messages:
deploy-bot: Deploybot alert: EU canary slice (region=eu) p95 latency spike 820ms (threshold 600ms). 5.2% error rate on model-service v2.3. Auto-rollback candidate: v2.2.9. Suggested action: PARTIAL_ROLLBACK(region=eu) unless human override within 5m.
Maya: saw the alert, thanks. can we get a quick histogram of seq lengths? might be batch/kv-cache regression.
Raj: grabbing traces, 10s window shows spikes align with long-context requests (~4096). KV cache miss rate jumped.
Tess: @Maya @Raj if it's KV cache related, rolling back model variant might help. can we limit to EU region only? customers in US unaffected.
Jim: +1 limit to eu. Do we have release notes updated for v2.3? need to mention kv cache heuristics change.
Olivia: drafting a brief for affected customers now. if we rollback EU, will notify subset.
Maya: hold auto-rollback for 3m while we confirm root cause. if KV cache flag is the culprit, we can toggle flag instead of rollback.
deploy-bot: Ack. Holding auto-rollback. countdown 3m. will re-evaluate.
Raj: confirmed: code change in model runtime switched to aggressive kv prefetch; causes regression on long sequences under specific batch sizes. Repro locally with this command: `./run_infer --model v2.3 --seq 4096 --batch 4` yields p95 ~900ms.
Tess: can we flip the prefetch flag? `rwctl feature toggle runtime.kv_prefetch=false --env eu` — would that be less disruptive?
Maya: good idea. Raj, how fast is a flag toggle?
Raj: ~30s to propagate across nodes. would avoid client-facing version change. but need approval for emergency config push.
Jim: ops, prefer config toggle over a rollback, lower blast radius. any risk of increased error rate after toggle?
Raj: minor risk: some throughputs might drop slightly but errors should drop.
Olivia: proceeding to update customer note draft to say: "We identified a regression affecting long-context requests in EU; engineers are applying a config change to mitigate. We'll follow up if rollback is needed."
Support Bot: Created incident INC-2026; notifying on-call and account owners for top 5 customers in eu.
Maya: ok deploy config toggle then monitor for 10m. if p95 > 650ms or errors > 2% rollback to v2.2.9 for EU only. who will run the rollback if toggle fails?
Tess: I can run rollback. rollback command: `rwctl release rollback --region eu --to-version 2.2.9 --scope canary,dedicated` — will only affect routing in eu.
Jim: ensure release-notes link and changelog pinned: update release notes with the mitigation steps and exec plan.
Raj: toggled runtime.kv_prefetch=false in eu. propagation logs: `kv_prefetch=false applied on 12/12 nodes`
deploy-bot: Re-eval: p95 dropped to 480ms, error-rate 0.9% in last 2m. condition cleared. Auto-rollback cancelled.
Maya: great work. leave the toggle for now, schedule a hotfix for the prefetch heuristic. open PR: "runtime: conservative kv prefetch by default" and tag for 2.3.1.
Tess: PR created: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/2345 — assign Raj.
Olivia: customer emails sent to affected accounts, included link to incident and workaround note.
Support Bot: INC-2026 updated: RESOLVED (mitigated via config toggle).
Maya: postmortem: short blameless doc please — include timeline, roll decision tree, and whether rollback would have been safer. Action items: (1) add canary gating on kv_prefetch changes, (2) add p95-by-seqlen alert, (3) release notes checklist for infra changes.
Jim: I'll draft the release-note addendum and the rollback runbook addition (commands, contacts, comm template).
Tess: moving to close. thanks all :thumbsup:
Olivia: tnx everyone, will follow up with customers in 24h.
